A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UQ evaluation study. Their main texts, figures, table, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original UQ benchmarks across four datasets and four models, correlation analyses, and human evaluation of 450 responses with four annotations each.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and human-evaluation results and adds Semantic Entropy comparisons and threshold-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The work remains an evaluation study using established UQ estimators and correctness functions. The added Semantic Entropy variants are comparison methods; no proposed algorithm, architecture, or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate QA on TriviaQA, SQuAD, NQ-Open, and SimpleQA, retaining context-provided SQuAD and closed-book evaluation elsewhere. Human evaluation covers the same three datasets excluding SQuAD. Other confounders and verbalized uncertainty are discussed without new task evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 adds Semantic Entropy with and without length normalization to Figure 1 and the correlation comparison, increasing the stated UQ method count from six to eight. The existing estimators, token/character-length baselines, and correctness functions remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds correctness-threshold sweeps across 0–1 and comparisons between normalized and unnormalized Semantic Entropy. The original model configurations, prompts, greedy decoding, fixed-threshold benchmarks, and human-annotation sample sizes remain documented as before.

E4.justification: V1 examines selected thresholds and length relationships; v2 adds systematic human-agreement sensitivity curves for five correctness functions across three datasets in Figure 8, with an excerpt in Figure 3. This substantially expands the evidence about threshold robustness and whether suitable thresholds transfer across datasets. The length-correlation analysis also includes both Semantic Entropy variants.

E5.justification: Both retain four annotations per response and the same Cohen's kappa and Spearman correlation reporting practices. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its additional curves use the existing agreement statistic.

E6.justification: Figure 2's overall agreement matrix changes substantially: the first annotator's AlignScore cell changes from 65 to 82 as displayed, while the dataset-specific appendix matrices remain identical. V2 adds Semantic Entropy AUROCs, correlations, and threshold-sweep results. Some retained correlations also change, including token length versus the ROUGE-trained probe from -0.8 to -0.7.

T1.justification: Appendix C's assumptions and derivation are unchanged apart from a citation and equation numbering. However, Section 2.4 changes the independent-error statement from preserving expected method rankings to calling AUROC an unbiased estimator. This is a different mathematical property and conflicts with the appendix's retained bias-toward-0.5 result; no new proof resolves it.

C1.justification: V2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion foreground a claimed formal proof that any mutual bias systematically distorts AUROC evaluations and rankings, presenting length as one instance. V1's central contribution emphasizes the empirical diagnosis of correctness-function and length biases. This substantially broadens the central claimed contribution, although the general appendix analysis already existed.

C2.justification: V2 explains how poor thresholds produce nearly constant labels and why optimal thresholds differ across datasets. New Section 4 hypothesizes vocabulary/style confounding when verbalized uncertainty is combined with LM judges. General warnings about other confounders and validating judges against humans already appear in v1, so those are retained qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A documents Semantic Entropy clustering and its normalization variants, while Appendix D identifies DeBERTa as the NLI component and adds a link to the existing Farquhar evaluation implementation. The original prompts, model identifiers, probe optimizer settings, and annotation guidelines are retained; no new author-code release is established.

R1.justification: Appendix C newly acknowledges Ielanskyi et al. (2025) as concurrent work with a similar AUROC analysis. Section 4 adds connections to verbalized-uncertainty and judge-style-bias research, and Appendix B adds the RoBERTa citation. Most prior positioning remains, with bibliographic consolidation rather than substantive removal of existing works.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, introduction, error-analysis discussion, and conclusion, inserts Beyond Length Bias, renames Section 3.3, and shortens bibliographic entries. Most background material, experimental organization, and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the threshold plots in Figure 8 and their main-text excerpt in Figure 3, expands Figure 1's bars and legend, and enlarges the correlation matrix. Existing scatterplots and dataset-specific agreement panels are retained and renumbered. Table 1 and the overall visual style remain, with local layout changes including the annotation-guideline box.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens the empirical case through systematic threshold sweeps, relevant Semantic Entropy comparisons, and replacement of v1's main agreement matrix that duplicated the SimpleQA panel. These benefits are limited by introduced theoretical imprecision: the stronger proof framing adds no new derivation, and Section 2.4's new unbiased-estimator claim contradicts Appendix C's retained bias-toward-0.5 result.
